column1: # French grammar words. One line per word as written + part of speech:
# word <TAB> UD part of speech <TAB> senses separated by " | ".
# The file replaces Wiktionary's determiner, pronoun, preposition, conjunction,
# particle and auxiliary entries for every word listed here; nouns, verbs,
# adverbs and other content words stay (`la` the note, `pas` "step"), unless a
# line lists that part of speech too. A word's lines come first in the popover,
# in this file's order, so its commonest use goes first. Case matters.
# Irregular verb forms a reader can't connect to their infinitive get lines of
# their own (`va` "goes", `peut` "can"): the protocol has no inflection tables.
# "→ aller" links the line to its verb, which the popover still shows after it;
# a VERB line replaces Wiktionary's other verbs for the word (`vader` for `va`).
# Each sense explains what the word does, for a learner reading it next to
# the sentence: what it expresses, then the English, then a short phrase in
# brackets when the English alone doesn't settle it ("à and le joined: to the: to the station (au bureau)"). No notes
# on case or position: the sentence shows those.
# A form names its base word, which links it: "form of aller: goes → aller".
